chunks: And if you ask them, 'Who created the heavens and the earth?' they will surely say, 'God.' Say, 'Then have you considered what you invoke besides God? If God intends harm for me, are they able to remove His harm? Or if He intends mercy for me, are they able to withhold His mercy?' Say, 'Sufficient for me is God; upon Him let the trusting place their trust.'
ai.seo_question: What is the logical argument used in the Quran to refute the worship of false gods alongside God?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse highlights the logical inconsistency of polytheists who acknowledge Allah as the Creator yet attribute independent agency to idols, a critique central to the concept of Tawhid al-Uluhiyyah. The rhetorical question emphasizes that divine decree (Qadr) is absolute, rendering intermediaries powerless to alter harm or mercy, thereby urging believers to direct their ultimate reliance (Tawakkul) exclusively to Allah.
